labels.label: theo:steiner_2

hypotheses.note: x : ℤ, 0 < n, T^[n] x = x. n need not be the minimal period. a_i is read as a_i(x_0) = ν₂(3T^i(x_0)+1), extended n-periodically to ℤ: any periodic α with α k = a_k(x) on ℕ (OQ-68 (a)).

A reading: per period, #(𝒟 ∩ ⟦0, n−1⟧) = 1, i.e. ((range n).filter (1 < α ·)).card = 1. Every window ⟦c, c+n−1⟧ gives the same count (card_filter_desc_window), so ⟦1, n⟧ of l.306 is the same hypothesis. The literal reading (encard of the subset 𝒟_Γ ⊆ ℤ) is SteinerTwoLiteralStmt and is vacuous (finding 1).
Read as '1 is a term of the cycle', ∃ k, T^[k] x = 1. On a cycle this is x = 1 (exists_iterate_eq_one_iff_of_cycle).

As printed (any cycle of ℤ) the statement is refuted (steinerTwo_printed_false). The true forms add a hypothesis and are not the anchor: x > 0 and n ≤ 100 (steinerTwo_pos_of_le); any sign and n ≤ 100, with conclusion Γ ∈ {(1), (−5, −7)} (steinerTwo_int_of_le); n = 1, any sign, as printed (steinerTwo_period_one). For x > 0 and every n, the statement is shown equivalent to SteinerArithStmt (steinerTwoPos_iff_arith), which is not assumed. OQ-63 (a).

The base point moves to the point after the unique descending index (steiner_point). The displays are proved for every n-periodic α ≥ 1 with 𝒟 ∩ ⟦1, n−1⟧ = ∅ (weakened: α_0 = 1 is allowed where unused).
Both readings: Aun (printed) and AunAlt (product to n − 2 − k), in every display and in the bound.
The displays on sequences need no convention. On a cycle both conventions are covered: α_k = a_k(x), l.62 (steiner_m_cycle), and β_{k+1} = a_k(x), l.71 (steiner_m_cycle_shift).
SEquiv (x = s·y, s ∈ S, in ℚ). steiner_delta gives the factors explicitly (2^{n−1}, 3·2^{n−1}, 2·3^{n−2}, 2·3^{n−1}), so every reading of 'up to a factor in S' is covered.
Read as p_n(x_0) = ∑_{t<n} a_t, the sum over one period, as l.302's 2^α = 2^{|Γ|−n} and l.167's count of cycles by (|Γ|, n) require.

hypotheses.paper: the corollary to Matveev's theorem (cor:property_defined_cycles_gcd) and the computer check (l.302)
hypotheses.note: Neither is stated, assumed or named as an external. The bound the corollary consumes is proved (steiner_gcd_bound, steiner_corollary_hypothesis). The theorem on positive cycles is proved equivalent to SteinerArithStmt, the arithmetic statement both steps are used to settle (steinerTwoPos_iff_arith). The check runs in the kernel for n ≤ 100 (steinerArith_check_pos, steinerArith_check_neg).

findings: syracuse.tex:295 — '#𝒟_Γ = 1' read literally is never satisfied. 𝒟_Γ ⊆ ℤ is n-periodic, so it is empty or infinite (Syracuse.encard_descIdx_ne_one), and the literal statement holds vacuously (steinerTwoLiteral_vacuous). The count is per period, as the proof's 'Assume 𝒟 = nℤ' (l.298) and the '#(𝒟_Γ ∩ ⟦1, n⟧)' of theo:syracuse_cycle (l.306) read it.

syracuse.tex:294–295 — false over ℤ as printed. The cycle (−5, −7) has a = (1, 2), so one descending index per period, and 1 is not a term (Syracuse.steinerTwo_neg_five, steinerTwo_printed_false). It holds for n = 1 over ℤ (steinerTwo_period_one). For n ≤ 100, the n-cycles of ℤ with one descending index per period are exactly (1) and (−5, −7) (steinerTwo_int_of_le, both sides checked in the kernel), and the positive ones are (1) only (steinerTwo_pos_of_le).

syracuse.tex:150 against 294 — the planner's (c), confirmed in Lean. theo:steiner (cited, l.150) and theo:steiner_2 on positive cycles are the same statement (Syracuse.steiner_iff_steinerTwoPos). theo:steiner's '∀ k < n, p_k(x) = k' is a_0 = ⋯ = a_{n−2} = 1 at the point after the descending index (steiner_point, p_eq_self_of_a_eq_one). Both are equivalent to the arithmetic statement 'n ≥ 1, 3^n < 2^{n+e}, 2^{n+e} − 3^n ∣ 2^e − 1 ⇒ n = e = 1' (SteinerArithStmt, steinerTwoPos_iff_arith). The reduction is exact: every solution with e ≥ 1 is an n-cycle of the required shape (steiner_cycle_of_dvd). So the paper proves at l.294–303, through the corollary to Matveev's theorem, the result it cites at l.150.

syracuse.tex:298–301 — the exact reduction behind the proof (the planner's (3)). With y the point after the descending index and α = a_{n−1}(y) − 1: p_n = n + α, y(2^{n+α} − 3^n) = 3^n − 2^n (lem:base) and 2^{n+α} − 3^n ∣ 2^α − 1, for either sign (Syracuse.steiner_reduction). For y > 0 also α ≥ 1 and 3^n < 2^{n+α} ≤ 3^n + 2^α − 1 < 2·3^n (steiner_reduction_pos, steiner_cycle_pos).

syracuse.tex:298 — 'm = A_0 ∧ Δ_{−1}'. For every n-periodic α ≥ 1 with 𝒟 ⊆ nℤ, the common divisors of A_0 and Δ_{−1} are those of all the A_u, for both readings of OQ-43 (Syracuse.steiner_gcd_alt_iff, steiner_gcd_aun_iff). On a cycle, the OQ-43 reading gives A'_0 ∧ Δ'_{−1} = |2^{p_n} − 3^n|, which is the printed m for x > 0, in both index conventions (steiner_m_cycle, steiner_m_cycle_shift). For the printed A_u^n, A_0 ∧ Δ_{−1} = GCD(A_u) = 2|2^{p_n} − 3^n| when n ≥ 2 (gcd_Aun_of_cycle_of_asc), so never 2^{p_n} − 3^n. In that reading m is even and does not divide the odd 2^α − 1. The proof's implicit step from 'Δ ∼_S 2^α − 1' to m ∣ 2^α − 1 needs m prime to 6, which holds only in the OQ-43 reading (2^{p_n} − 3^n is odd and prime to 3). The bound of l.302 holds in both readings, up to a factor 2.

syracuse.tex:299 — the planner's (a), confirmed. 'α = a_0 − 1 = ½(|a(Γ)| − n)' has a spurious ½. |a(Γ)| = n + α (Syracuse.steiner_sum_eq), so α = |a(Γ)| − n, as l.302 itself writes it. The printed identity fails whenever a_0 > 1 (steiner_alpha_half_false), e.g. at the cycle (1): α = 1 against ½.

syracuse.tex:301 — 'Δ_1 ∼_S 2^α − 1' holds exactly for n ≥ 2, for both readings of OQ-43, at i = 1 as printed and at i = −1 (the index of l.298). Δ'_1 = 2^{n−1}(2^α − 1), Δ_1 = 3·2^{n−1}(2^α − 1), Δ'_{−1} = 2·3^{n−2}(2^α − 1), Δ_{−1} = 2·3^{n−1}(2^α − 1) (Syracuse.steiner_delta, steiner_delta_sEquiv). It fails for n = 1, at the cycle (1) itself: there every Δ_i = 0, while 2^α − 1 = 1 (steiner_delta_period_one_false). The conclusion m ∣ 2^α − 1 still holds there, by lem:base.

syracuse.tex:302 — the planner's (b), confirmed. '2^{|Γ|−n} ≤ 2^{|Γ|(1−log₃2)}' (|Γ| = p_n) is equivalent to 2^{p_n} ≤ 3^n. On a cycle of ℤ it holds iff the cycle is negative, so it is reversed on every positive cycle (Syracuse.steiner_printed_bound_iff). The form that holds, from 2^{p_n} < 2·3^n: 2^α < 2^{log₃2}·2^{|Γ|(1−log₃2)} (steiner_bound). The corollary's '≪' absorbs the constant.

syracuse.tex:162, 302 — the hypothesis of the corollary to Matveev's theorem is proved for 𝒫(Γ) = 'Γ positive with one descending index per period', with ε = log₃2 and an explicit constant, for both readings of OQ-43. GCD(A'_u) = 2^{p_n} − 3^n ≤ 2^α − 1 < 2^{log₃2}·2^{|Γ|(1−ε)}, and GCD(A_u) ≤ 2^{α+1} (Syracuse.steiner_gcd_bound). In the corollary's form, ∃ ε ∈ (0, 1), ∃ C, with C = 2^{1+log₃2} (steiner_corollary_hypothesis).

syracuse.tex:302, 'with the aid of a computer' — the check runs in the kernel (decide) for n ≤ 100. On the positive side the only solution is (n, α) = (1, 1), i.e. x = 1. On the negative side it is (2, 1), i.e. x = −5 (Syracuse.steinerArith_check_pos, steinerArith_check_neg). This confirms the planner's [r] numerics in that range. They were re-run, not as a proof, for n < 400, with the same two solutions.
questions: '#𝒟_Γ = 1' (l.295): per period, #(𝒟_Γ ∩ ⟦0, n−1⟧) = 1, or the literal cardinal of the subset of ℤ? Reading taken: per period (SteinerTwoStmt). The literal reading is stated (SteinerTwoLiteralStmt) and shown vacuous.

Are § 3's cycles positive (OQ-63 (a))? If so, the statement of record is SteinerTwoPosStmt. It is equivalent to theo:steiner (l.150) and to SteinerArithStmt, and proved for n ≤ 100. Over ℤ it is false, and the corrected conclusion would be 'Γ is (1) or (−5, −7)', proved for n ≤ 100. Reading taken: none ruled; both forms are stated.

Is theo:steiner_2 meant as an independent proof of theo:steiner (l.150), which it restates for x > 0, or as its § 3 restatement? Reading taken: the two are proved equivalent. Neither is assumed, and only theo:steiner_2's own steps are formalized.
|a(Γ)| (l.299) and |Γ| (l.302): the sum p_n of a over one period? Reading taken: yes. With |Γ| the number of points, 2^{|Γ|−n} = 1 and l.302 says nothing.
Δ_1 (l.301) or Δ_{−1} (l.298–299)? The argument needs the index of l.299. Reading taken: both, proved for n ≥ 2 with explicit factors (steiner_delta). For n = 1 neither holds.
'Γ = (⋯,1,⋯)' (l.295, l.302): 1 is a term of the cycle? Reading taken: yes, ∃ k, T^k(x) = 1, which on a cycle is x = 1.

m at l.298, '2^{p_n} − 3^n' or 'GCD(A_i)' (OQ-68 (c), (d)), and which A_i (OQ-43)? Reading taken: all four combinations are computed (steiner_m_cycle). They agree, as the printed m, only for the OQ-43 reading on positive cycles.
∼_S (l.301; OQ-68 (c)): x = s·y with s ∈ S, in ℚ? Reading taken: SEquiv, with the factor in S given explicitly, so any reading of 'up to a factor in S' is covered.

The index convention for a_i (OQ-63 (b)): l.62 or l.71? Reading taken: both. The displays on sequences need no convention; the cycle form of l.298 is proved in both (steiner_m_cycle, steiner_m_cycle_shift).

kb_proposals: One descending index per period (theo:steiner_2): steiner_point moves to y = T^{d+1}(x), the point after the descending index, where a_0 = ⋯ = a_{n−2} = 1 and a_{n−1} = α + 1 (theo:steiner's p_k = k). steiner_reduction gives y(2^{n+α} − 3^n) = 3^n − 2^n and 2^{n+α} − 3^n ∣ 2^α − 1, for either sign. steiner_cycle_of_dvd is the converse: it builds the cycle from the divisor, with X_u = A'_u/D (odd) and T_unique at each step (SyracuseScaffold.Steiner).

A bounded kernel check of a Diophantine statement: decide on '∀ n < 101, ∀ e < 2n, … % … = 0 → …' over ℕ runs in about 5 s. It needs set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1024, since otherwise the Decidable instance of five nested implications is not found. It needs maxRecDepth 100000 from n ≈ 80. It needs exponentiation.threshold 1024, since otherwise it warns, which is an error under warningAsError (steinerArith_check_pos).

Pitfall: in Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun t ht => by rw [h]; exact …) with no target given, the target function is a metavariable. rw then closes the goal by rfl and assigns it, so nothing is rewritten ('no goals' on the exact). State the target sum first, or pass (g := …).

Powers of 2 against powers of 3 with logb: Real.rpow_le_rpow_left_iff or rpow_lt_rpow_of_exponent_lt reduce to the exponents. Real.log_div_log turns logb 3 2 into log 2 / log 3, then div_le_iff₀ and Real.log_le_log_iff with Real.log_pow give an integer power inequality (steiner_printed_bound_iff, steiner_bound).
notes: One file, scaffold/SyracuseScaffold/Steiner.lean (module SyracuseScaffold.Steiner). It imports only Syracuse.UpperBounds (and through it Mathlib and the strict modules), and nothing of TwoDescents. 44 declarations, 0 sorry, no axiom, no native_decide. `lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true` exits 0 with no output. `taskset -c 0-11 lake build SyracuseScaffold.Steiner` built only this module (2187 jobs; the strict oleans are unchanged: Base/Valuation 2026-11-20 19:53, Rep/IntegerBounds 23:01, Completion 2026-11-21 00:01, CycleGcd 02:21, UpperBounds 04:56). #print axioms of all 44 declarations, from a /tmp copy: 41 depend on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and steinerArith_check_pos, steinerArith_check_neg and SteinerArithStmt on [propext]. The two kernel checks carry set_option maxRecDepth / synthInstance.maxSize / exponentiation.threshold ... in (about 5 s each; the whole file takes about 7 s). No label is marked. The row stays partial: it waits on T-syr-cited, OQ-63 (a) and OQ-68. The scaffold root SyracuseScaffold.lean does not import the new module. Every declaration name was grepped against Syracuse/ (Completion.lean included) with no clash. The generic helper names to check against T-syr-two-descents at graduation are exists_iterate_eq_one_iff_of_cycle, card_filter_desc_window, encard_descIdx_ne_one, p_iterate_eq_of_cycle, p_eq_self_of_a_eq_one, periodic_sub_one_of_desc, gcd_Aun_of_cycle_of_asc and AunAlt_shift_one. SteinerStmt is the statement of theo:steiner (l.150), a label of T-syr-cited. It is stated only so that the planner's (c) can be proved as an equivalence. It is neither assumed nor proved, and it should not anchor theo:steiner without that target's ruling. SteinerArithStmt is not a cited result: it is the arithmetic statement the two cited steps of l.302 settle, and it appears only as the right-hand side of an equivalence; steiner_eq_one_of_arith takes it inline, at one n. Suggested anchors, if a ruling makes the row closable: steinerTwoPos_iff_arith with steiner_iff_steinerTwoPos (the exact reduction), steiner_corollary_hypothesis (what the corollary consumes), steinerTwo_printed_false (the refutation) and steinerTwo_int_of_le (the corrected statement over ℤ for n ≤ 100).
